notes: An antibody may recognize an epitope on more than one product form or a remaining fragment. Many mass-spectrometry workflows digest proteins into peptides: a shared detected peptide cannot distinguish every full-length form. A candidate peptide sequence also does not establish its display by HLA. Separate assays address amount, location, intact form, function and antigen presentation.

records.name: Receptor
records.tldr: Receptors connect molecular recognition to a cellular response through several mechanisms. Their presence and their activity are separate findings.
records.summary: Receptors can be on the surface or inside a cell. Ligand-gated ion channels regulate ion passage; G-protein-coupled receptors act through G proteins; enzyme-linked receptors can contain an enzyme or recruit a separate one. Intracellular nuclear receptors can regulate transcription with cellular partners. A surface signal can ultimately alter genes, while nuclear-receptor family membership does not fix every molecule permanently in the nucleus or require every effect to use new transcription.

notes: Defined engineered estrogen-receptor experiments detected nuclear and membrane pools; they do not establish a universal proportion in human tumors. Distinguish receptor identity, location, accessible binding and measured function. A positive stain or fluorescence intensity is not automatically a calibrated receptor count, pathway dependence or drug sensitivity.

HER2 is an orphan receptor without a known direct activating ligand. Its partner HER3 binds neuregulin. Diwanji and colleagues studied the HER2-HER3-NRG1-beta complex, including defined mutant and purified-complex experiments, so a generic growth factor drawn directly on HER2 would assign the wrong binding partner. Antibody binding, disruption of an assembled complex and inhibition of activation are separate outcomes; the mutant-complex results do not define every antibody response in an unmodified tumour.

records.name: Regulatory T cells
records.tldr: Some T cells restrain immune responses and help protect healthy tissues. Their presence alone does not measure suppression.
records.summary:
Regulatory T cells help maintain self-tolerance and can restrain antitumour responses. Mouse experiments established a regulatory role for CD4/CD25 populations and linked Foxp3 to the regulatory programme. CTLA-4 can remove CD80/CD86 from antigen-presenting cells, reducing support available to other T cells. This is one mechanism, rather than a complete account of every regulatory population.

In defined human cultures, induced FOXP3 expression did not confer suppressive function. Human colorectal cancers also contained functionally distinct FOXP3-positive populations. FOXP3 staining alone therefore does not establish suppression or a universal prognosis; CD25 also needs identity and activation context. Use a defined marker panel, tissue location and controlled suppression assays. Mixed RNA signatures do not locate every contributing cell. Regulatory cells are not exhausted effectors, and removing restraint does not automatically provide safe clinical benefit.

links.label: Immunologic self-tolerance maintained by activated T cells expressing IL-2 receptor alpha-chains (CD25). Breakdown of a single mechanism of self-tolerance causes various autoimmune diseases.
Control of regulatory T cell development by the transcription factor Foxp3.
Trans-endocytosis of CD80 and CD86: a molecular basis for the cell-extrinsic function of CTLA-4.
Induction of FOXP3 expression in naive human CD4+FOXP3 T cells by T-cell receptor stimulation is transforming growth factor-beta dependent but does not confer a regulatory phenotype.
Two FOXP3(+)CD4(+) T cell subpopulations distinctly control the prognosis of colorectal cancers.

notes: Regulatory T cells are living, context-dependent populations, commonly within CD4, that protect tolerance and may restrain useful antitumour responses. They can develop through thymic or peripheral routes. They are not exhausted effectors. Removing restraint can damage healthy tissue; cell abundance is not a universal prognostic or treatment rule.

Regulatory mechanisms include CTLA-4-mediated loss of supporting ligands and context-dependent cytokine and growth-signal interactions, including IL-2. Counting cells does not measure suppression. Flow cytometry combines markers, multiplex tissue imaging adds location and a controlled suppression assay measures a specified responder endpoint. Preserve specimen, marker and comparator definitions; bulk RNA cannot assign every cell a location or function, and none of these methods supplies a universal clinical cutoff.

records.name: Drug resistance (primary and acquired)
records.tldr: A cancer may respond less to a medicine from the start or after an earlier response. The cause can involve cell populations, drug exposure or several mechanisms.
records.summary: Drug resistance describes reduced treatment effect in a specified setting. Primary and acquired resistance describe the timing of response, rather than proving a single biological cause. Changes in the target, alternative signalling, drug handling and reversible cell states can contribute. Sampling, exposure and controlled functional evidence are needed to distinguish a plausible explanation from a demonstrated treatment-specific mechanism.

links.label: Wikipedia
NCI: targeted cancer therapies, resistance and adverse effects
Sharma et al.: reversible drug-tolerant states in cancer-cell models (2010)
Sakai et al.: BRCA2 depletion and resistance in ovarian cancer models (2009)

notes: Drug resistance is reduced effect for a specified medicine, cancer population and setting. A garden analogy can describe selection: removing susceptible plants leaves a larger share of survivors, without showing that the treatment created those survivors. Intrinsic resistance describes poor initial effect; acquired resistance describes lost effect after an earlier response. These timing labels do not identify one permanent mechanism. A rare pre-existing population can become easier to detect, and sequence change, reversible cell state, exposure and the surrounding tissue can contribute together.

NCI describes changes that prevent a medicine interacting with its target and alternative growth routes that no longer depend on that target. Investigation can also ask whether the required target is still present and accessible, whether drug efflux or inadequate local exposure changes the amount reaching cells, whether death signalling is bypassed, and whether the surrounding tissue changes exposure or survival. These are competing or coexisting hypotheses, rather than a mechanism established by a failed scan response. Cross-resistance needs evidence for the actual drugs and the attributed mechanism; a shared class name does not establish it.

Sharma 2010 found small drug-tolerant populations in human cancer-cell cultures. In PC9 lung cancer cells, persisters propagated without drug regained sensitivity within nine doublings; expanded persister populations required roughly 90 doublings or 20 to 30 passages. The observations supported a reversible chromatin-associated state in those systems, distinct from assuming a new permanent resistance mutation. They do not establish that a treatment break is safe or beneficial for a person. Drug withdrawal and re-exposure are experimental tests of reversibility, with matched conditions and controls.

A fictional population starts with 990 sensitive and 10 resistant cells, total 1,000. Removing 90 per cent of the sensitive cells leaves 99 sensitive plus 10 resistant cells, total 109. The resistant share rises from 10/1,000 = 1 per cent to 10/109, about 9.2 per cent, although the absolute resistant count stays at 10. No division, mutation or state switching is included. To display this honestly, compare absolute counts on one 0 to 1,000 scale and resistant fractions on a separately labelled 0 to 10 per cent scale. A larger fraction alone does not prove growth of that population, a newly induced mutation or a clinical treatment effect.

A useful investigation first checks exposure, assay performance and what the sample represents. It then compares earlier and later specimens, the sampled sites, coverage and detection limits, and candidate target, pathway, state or environmental changes. Controlled models can test target engagement, pathway activity, damage and survival separately. Genetic perturbation or rescue, an appropriate comparison compound, and removal/re-exposure can strengthen a causal explanation, but off-target effects and altered growth can confound it. Culture does not reproduce every tissue, immune, exposure or human-safety condition; clinical response assessment and mechanistic research remain distinct.

Combining drugs is a hypothesis that must address the measured failure at useful exposures and tolerable harm. NCI notes both the rationale for combinations and the possibility of serious targeted-treatment side effects. Different pathway targets do not guarantee nonoverlapping toxicity or clinical rescue. A later variant found in a fictional progression sample is especially hard to interpret if the earlier sample lacked enough coverage to detect it: it may have been present but undetected, arisen later or be unrelated to the observed failure. First check the comparison and detection limit, then test its treatment-specific function. Detection, origin, timing and causation are separate conclusions.

In a fictional matched comparison, model A retains the source antigen, peptide-HLA display and tested receptor recognition, but the same cytotoxic drug causes less target death than before. Model B loses the required display while retaining its measured response to that drug. These locate different failed requirements: drug response in A and the tested immune-recognition route in B. They do not identify the complete cause, show that every immune route has failed or select a replacement treatment. Compare earlier and later material with compatible assays and matched exposure.

Lung-cancer resistance investigations distinguish a changed drug target, bypass signalling and a change in tumour lineage. Finding a candidate mechanism does not by itself establish dependence on that pathway or specify a next medicine. A later-generation inhibitor, a combination or another treatment requires evidence for the exact alteration, previous exposure, disease setting and safety. Tissue and plasma sample different aspects of the disease, and a negative test is limited by sampling and assay sensitivity. The NCI overview supports the target-change and bypass distinction; the linked disease-specific papers provide separate cohorts rather than one universal frequency or switching rule.

records.name: Cellular senescence
records.tldr: Senescent cells remain alive while their division is durably arrested. Their effects depend on the cells, signals and surrounding tissue.
records.summary: Senescence is a stress-associated cell state with durable cell-cycle arrest and other context-dependent features. Identifying it requires combined measurements rather than one marker. In genetically switchable blood-cancer models, release from senescence allowed renewed division with enhanced clonogenic potential. That experimental result does not predict that every senescent cell will restart or that a person will relapse. Arrest, secretion and effects on neighbouring cells require separate assessment. Model findings do not establish a preferred senolytic treatment.

notes: Leading programmes: Lowe (MSK) on senescence and immune clearance; Campisi legacy (Buck); Kirkland (Mayo) on senolytics; Demaria (ERIBA Groningen); Peeper (NKI) on one-two punch.

Senescent cells remain alive and metabolically active while division is durably arrested. Damage, oncogenic signals and treatment stresses can induce the state. It is distinct from death, reversible quiescence, the broader concept of dormancy and immune exhaustion, and is not a synonym for a person's age.

Low proliferation and increased p21 one day after stress do not establish durable senescence or a harmful secretory programme. Combine cell identity, longitudinal arrest or regrowth assessment and complementary features such as p16, p21, damage markers and senescence-associated beta-galactosidase. Fixed tissue cannot test later recovery, and no universal marker or arrest-duration cutoff works across contexts. Research outputs include method-defined cell fractions, marker intensities and longitudinal proliferation or regrowth. Stained sections and tested cells consume material. Secretions and their functional effects require their own readouts rather than inference from an arrest marker.

The senescence-associated secretory phenotype varies with cell, stimulus, timing and environment. In Coppé and colleagues' culture experiments, selected secretions promoted epithelial invasiveness; in Demaria and colleagues' mouse skin wounds, senescent cells and PDGF-AA supported repair. Neither experiment establishes a universal harmful mixture or a clinical instruction to remove senescent cells.

Genetically switchable blood-cancer models showed enhanced clonogenic growth after release from senescence. This supports possible escape in those systems, not inevitable restart, relapse prediction or a preferred senolytic treatment. Arrest, secretion and effects on neighbouring cells require separate tests.
records.analogy: A workshop can stop making copies while continuing to use energy and send messages. The messages and their effects must be measured in context.
interventions: Experimental induction, persistence and clearance require separate measurements.
Model findings do not establish a preferred senolytic treatment.

records.tldr: T cells are immune cells with different recognition systems and roles. Their presence does not by itself show that they recognise or kill cancer.
records.summary: T cells develop through the thymus. Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognise peptide-HLA displays through a paired receptor; CD4 and CD8 identify major co-receptor populations, rather than fixed helper and killer jobs. Some human bladder-tumour CD4 cells showed class-II-dependent cytotoxicity in controlled experiments, while regulatory populations restrain responses. Identity, receptor specificity, state and measured function need separate evidence. A CD3 or CD8 stain establishes a sampled population under a defined panel, not tumour recognition or killing. Report compartment, viable-cell denominator, marker panel and timing. Controlled recognition and target-cell-death assays address different claims; cytokine production, division and treatment benefit are also separate outcomes.

Conventional alpha-beta cells recognise peptide-HLA; gamma-delta cells use another, context-dependent receptor system, so conventional peptide-HLA examples do not describe every T cell.

T-cell descriptions should separate identity, location, specificity, state and measured function. Flow cytometry uses defined viable-cell gates and panels, tissue staining adds location and sequencing adds receptor identity. Report compartment, denominator, panel and timing. CD3/CD8 positivity and a viral-peptide response establish their tested observations, not cancer recognition or killing by every nearby cell; greater presence or activation does not automatically mean clinical benefit.

records.name: T-cell exhaustion
records.tldr: Persistent stimulation can change a T cell's response programme. Exhausted populations contain subsets with different remaining functions and responses to checkpoint blockade.
records.summary: T-cell exhaustion is a distinct programme associated with persistent stimulation, multiple inhibitory receptors and altered transcription and chromatin. It is distinct from anergy and ordinary memory. Mouse experiments identified TOX as a central regulator. In chronic-infection and tumour models, progenitor exhausted populations retained response capacity and supplied descendants with different functions; terminally exhausted cells responded differently to anti-PD-1. A related melanoma association does not establish a universal treatment-selection test. PD-L1 blockade in mice re-engaged effector transcription with limited chromatin remodelling, and continued high antigen could lead to renewed exhaustion. Human skin-cancer studies also supported clonal replacement by clonotypes not previously detected in the sampled tumour. One marker, subset count or laboratory rescue does not establish tumour specificity, safe killing or individual clinical benefit.

notes: Exhaustion is a distinct differentiation programme associated with persistent stimulation, altered function, multiple inhibitory receptors and transcriptional and chromatin changes. Mouse TOX experiments identified a central regulator of this programme. It is neither brief tiredness, every weak assay, anergy nor a DNA sequence change. Deficits can be graded and subsets retain different capacities.

In chronic LCMV infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor exhausted cells self-renewed and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-L1 blockade. In Miller's mouse tumour experiments, progenitor cells persisted and expanded after PD-1 blockade, whereas terminally exhausted cells had greater immediate cytotoxicity against tested tumour targets. Persistence, capacity to divide after restimulation and immediate killing are different functions. The human melanoma component associated progenitor-like features with outcomes; it was not a universal predictive test, and terminally exhausted does not mean inert.

In mouse experiments, PD-L1 blockade re-engaged effector transcription with little remodelling of the exhausted chromatin landscape. Reinvigorated cells could become exhausted again under continued high antigen and did not simply become ordinary durable memory. Laboratory reinvigoration is distinct from universal reversal or patient benefit.

PD-1 can accompany activation as well as exhaustion. TCF1 also occurs in naive and memory contexts. TIM-3/CD39, TOX and residency-associated CD103/CD39 require population and assay context; no single marker assigns state or specificity. Combine compatible response history, protein or RNA programmes, receptor identities and controlled function. TOX may be measured by intracellular staining or RNA; this is not a routine universal pathology classifier.

Paired human basal-cell and squamous-cell skin-cancer biopsies after anti-PD-1 showed expanded clonotypes not previously observed in the same tumour. Clonal replacement and reinvigoration of resident cells are different, potentially overlapping response explanations. Non-detection before therapy is not proof of whole-body absence. Breast-cancer single-cell work identified checkpoint/effector-rich tissue-resident CD8 populations; its early TNBC survival signature was an association, not a general treatment predictor.
records.analogy: A response can change after repeated demands. The analogy stops at the biological programme: exhausted populations are heterogeneous, and remaining functions need measurement rather than a judgement that cells are broken.

records.name: T-cell priming and the three-signal model
records.tldr: A naive T cell's first activation depends on recognition and supporting signals. Division and killing are separate outcomes.
records.summary:
The three-signal teaching model groups peptide-HLA recognition by the T-cell receptor as signal one, costimulation as signal two and cytokine context as signal three. The naive cell already has its receptor. The model organises interacting processes; it is not a universal three-step checklist, and experienced or engineered cells can have different requirements.

Curtsinger and colleagues showed that type I interferons or IL-12 could support naive CD8 survival and effector differentiation in defined experiments. Proliferation without a third signal did not establish cytolytic function. Antigen presentation and initial priming are different processes. In a fictional matched comparison, two cultures each divide three times but only one kills appropriate targets above target-only background: equal division does not show equal function. Compare viable-cell input, peptide loading, HLA compatibility, cell ratios, exposure and positive and negative controls. Priming does not itself demonstrate natural tumour display, tumour access, safe killing or patient benefit.

notes: Priming is a naive cell's initial activation in a supporting context. Signal one is TCR recognition of peptide-HLA, signal two includes CD80/CD86-CD28 costimulation and inhibitory context, and signal three includes differentiation-supporting cytokines. The receptor pre-exists the encounter. These signals interact over time; the model is not a three-button checklist and antigen-experienced or engineered cells can have different requirements.

IL-12 and type I interferons (alpha/beta) supported naive CD8 survival and cytolytic differentiation in defined experiments. Cytokines are signalling proteins, not nutritional fuel. Type I interferon can connect innate responses to priming, but this does not prescribe a universal cytokine intervention or establish every cGAS-STING step. Dendritic-cell priming support and tumour antigen display answer different questions.

Division, viable-cell expansion, cytokine production and target-cell death are distinct priming outcomes. In a fictional matched experiment both cultures show three divisions, yet only B kills appropriate targets above target-only background. Measure these outcomes separately with defined starting cells, presenting system, signal perturbation, matched time, peptide loading, HLA, cell ratios and culture conditions. Priming does not establish tumour access, natural display, safe killing or clinical benefit, and stronger stimulation can support unwanted populations.

records.name: T-cell receptor
records.tldr: A conventional T-cell receptor recognises a peptide together with its HLA display. Recognition alone does not show killing.
records.summary:
A conventional alpha-beta T-cell receptor uses paired chains to recognise a peptide-HLA surface. Its recognition chains assemble with CD3 signalling partners, as demonstrated in the human TCR-CD3 structural study. CDR3 is an informative variable region, but neither a beta-chain sequence nor CDR3 alone specifies the complete paired receptor or its function.

Particular receptors can cross-react across peptide and HLA contexts; that does not establish a universal cross-reactivity rate. Paired receptor identity, binding, activation, target-cell death and clinical benefit require different evidence. A response by one reconstructed pair to peptide-loaded cells does not establish that another alpha-chain pairing recognises the same target, or that either kills naturally presenting tumour cells. Use irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls. Peptide loading can bypass natural processing, and contact diagrams are not healthy-tissue safety tests.

notes: A conventional alpha-beta TCR uses paired variable and constant domains to contact peptide plus HLA. The peptide sits in the HLA groove, not a separate TCR peptide pocket. CD3 signalling partners are distinct from recognition chains. Contact loops including junction-spanning CDR3 contribute, but other loops, the partner chain and HLA matter; beta-only or CDR3-only sequence is incomplete.

Cross-reactivity is recognition of multiple targets by a receptor. Defined receptor experiments demonstrated peptide/HLA cross-reactivity, not recognition of every allele by an arbitrary receptor or a universal rate. Greater affinity or a contact drawing does not establish healthy-tissue safety.

Sequencing reports sampled receptor identities and abundances under an operational clonotype definition. Paired alpha-beta identities are more complete than beta alone. Peptide-HLA multimer binding, stimulus-induced cellular response, target-cell death and clinical benefit are different endpoints. Include irrelevant-target, HLA and target-only viability controls; peptide-loaded cells can bypass natural processing.

Vaccination generally recruits or expands existing mature receptor specificities rather than rewriting each mature receptor. Engineered TCR therapy introduces selected receptor sequences. In either case, tested recognition must still connect to naturally presenting tumour targets, useful function and healthy-tissue safety. If one beta sequence pairs with different alpha chains, a positive reconstruction of one pair does not establish the other pair's function or tumour killing.

Many measured conventional receptor-peptide-HLA interactions have micromolar dissociation constants; affinity, multiple contacts, CD4/CD8 coreceptors and the cellular signalling context contribute differently to activity. Stone and colleagues review those distinctions, rather than a universal affinity ranking against every antibody. One receptor type per cell is also a simplification: extra productive alpha chains and dual surface receptors have been documented. A chain sequence alone does not establish which assembled receptor provides the measured specificity.

records.name: T-cell states
records.tldr: Response history and measured function help describe a T cell's state. One marker cannot provide a complete label.
records.summary:
Naive, effector, memory and exhausted populations describe response histories and differentiation programmes, not one mandatory sequence for every T cell. Anergy and exhaustion are distinct mechanisms. Regulatory function is a separate role. Identity, location, receptor specificity, state and measured function are complementary observations.

In chronic viral infection in mice, TCF1-associated progenitor populations sustained responses and supplied the proliferative burst after PD-1 blockade. In tumour models, progenitor exhausted cells differed from terminally exhausted cells; the related melanoma observations were associations rather than a universal treatment-selection rule. Progenitor-like exhaustion is not ordinary memory. A shared receptor does not require a shared functional phenotype, and PD-1 or TCF1 alone does not establish state or tumour specificity.

Paired human skin-cancer biopsies after PD-1 blockade showed expanded clonotypes not previously observed in the same tumour, supporting clonal replacement as another response model. Absence from an earlier sample does not establish absence throughout the body. A fictional PD-1-positive population near cancer can include viral-reactive and tumour-peptide-reactive cells. Neither proximity nor peptide response proves natural tumour recognition or killing. Preserve response history, sampling site, time, multiple markers and controlled function; neither division nor a favourable pattern predicts individual benefit.

Effector denotes developed response functions, including help or killing; memory can support renewed responses but promises neither permanent protection nor cancer specificity. State categories are not one mandatory developmental trajectory. Anergy, exhaustion, external suppression and regulatory role remain distinct.

The same paired receptor can occur with different functional phenotypes and response histories. Fictional R1 memory-associated and progenitor-like exhausted observations are separate observations, not a measured transition. Progenitor-like exhaustion is distinct from ordinary memory; shared TCF1 or division does not make their programmes equivalent.

Two fictional six-symbol PD-1-positive populations near cancer have different controlled peptide responses: one viral and one tumour-peptide directed. Marker and proximity do not establish specificity; peptide response does not establish natural tumour display, access or killing. Checkpoint blockade does not rewrite receptor specificity. Preserve tissue, sampling time, population definitions and controlled function alongside RNA/protein panels; favourable markers or division alone cannot predict benefit.

In Burger and colleagues' engineered mouse lung tumours, the subdominant response contained heterogeneous TCF1-positive populations, including a CCR6/Tc17-associated subset that did not preferentially benefit from checkpoint blockade. Long-peptide vaccination with the two model antigens and cyclic di-GMP improved the subdominant response; a subdominant-only arm also tested antigen-specific effects. The separate human analyses were associations, not a validated universal TCF1/CCR6 requirement, target-deletion rule or clone-pruning instruction.

Reduced division and immediate effector activity are separate measurements. In healthy-donor CD8 subsets, Henson and colleagues measured reduced proliferation alongside cytokine, perforin and granzyme expression; that protein panel alone is not a direct target-death assay, and not every EMRA cell carried the measured senescence markers. Pereira and colleagues separately demonstrated killing by defined senescent-like CD27-negative/CD28-negative CD8 cells, including MHC-I-deficient targets and NKG2D-DAP12-associated NK-like activity. These observations do not establish conventional tumour-specific TCR killing, durable control or clinical benefit for every highly differentiated cell.

records.name: TCR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: TCR-T supplies living T cells carrying a selected receptor that recognizes a specified peptide with its presenting HLA molecule. A source-protein name alone does not establish that target.
records.summary:
Conventional alpha-beta TCR-T introduces selected paired receptor-chain instructions into therapeutic T cells. The receptor recognizes a displayed peptide-HLA complex, rather than entering the tumor cell to bind the whole source protein. Natural processing, the required HLA allele, surface display, receptor expression and useful cell function remain different questions. This differs from administering a soluble TCR/CD3 protein that recruits other T cells.

Afamitresgene autoleucel (Tecelra) is an approved TCR-T example. FDA initially approved it in 2024 and converted the specified adult use to traditional approval in June 2026, extending the indication to patients aged 12 and older. Its synovial-sarcoma indication retains prior-chemotherapy, selected HLA and MAGE-A4 testing requirements. The full label also contains exclusions and safety requirements; a broad HLA-A*02 label is not a complete eligibility rule.

Introducing selected recognition instructions differs from expanding a tumor-derived population with its existing receptors. Viral transduction describes a delivery method, not the definition of every receptor-engineering process.

The conventional receptor uses paired alpha and beta chains alongside the CD3 complex. Cloning selected receptor coding sequences means copying instructions; one sequenced chain does not establish a complete functional receptor or its specificity. Expression and assembly in the finished cells require evaluation. The Dong structural study distinguishes recognition chains from associated signaling components. Bendle showed in mouse models that introduced and endogenous chains could form self-reactive mixed receptors; vector and cell-population changes reduced that model risk. This does not supply a clinical risk rate for every TCR-T product.

Protein expression and HLA typing lie upstream of the displayed ligand. Antigen/HLA loss or impaired presentation can remove one recognition route; retaining another allele does not rescue a receptor requiring the lost allele. A different receptor using a retained allele needs its own specificity and functional evidence.

In research, test paired receptor expression and naturally presenting targets, with relevant antigen/HLA removal and restoration, irrelevant peptides, unmodified effectors and healthy tissue. Multimer or peptide-loaded reagent binding is different from natural processing, target-cell death or patient benefit. This research validation is distinct from the approved product’s clinical testing rule.

Cameron investigated fatal cardiac toxicity with one affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 receptor and identified a cross-reactive Titin peptide presented by HLA-A*01 as the most likely cause. Earlier screening had not detected the hazard. This was a different receptor from the MAGE-A4 product Tecelra; stronger binding does not establish improved specificity or safety for either a new construct or an entire family.

The June 2026 Tecelra label names HLA-A*02:01P, -A*02:02P, -A*02:03P and -A*02:06P and a MAGE-A4 tumor test in its indication, with a separate HLA-A*02:05P contraindication. The approval letter documents the adult conversion and pediatric expansion. These are product-specific regulatory scopes, not a general rule for every TCR-T.

Conventional surface-antigen CARs and peptide-HLA-directed receptors have different recognition requirements, but peptide-HLA CARs also exist. The WT1/HLA-A*24:02 CAR study is a preclinical counterexample to saying all intracellular source antigens are unreachable by any CAR. A format change does not supply a missing required peptide-HLA complex.

For a soluble TCR/CD3 protein, the dosed molecule supplies recognition and recruits available T cells. TCR-T instead supplies receptor-bearing living cells. Protein exposure, cell trafficking/persistence and useful target-dependent function need separate measurements; neither format wins by definition.

In a fictional target cell, HLA allele A is lost while B remains. An A-restricted receptor loses that route; a B-restricted receptor still needs its own peptide to be processed and displayed. B2M is the shared light chain for many class-I complexes, whereas class-II HLA uses different alpha and beta chains. Neither one lost allele nor a change in interferon-induced display establishes complete loss of baseline presentation. Test the required allele, antigen and display conditions with matched viable targets rather than infer recognition from the HLA label. A conventional surface-antigen CAR has another dependency, and reduced class I alone does not guarantee NK-cell killing.

Selecting and expanding native antigen-reactive cells retains their existing receptors; introducing selected receptor coding sequences is receptor engineering. The two approaches can share discovery assays while differing in manufacturing and product-specific safety and release requirements. A banked research aliquot or a favourable receptor result alone does not establish that a viable, suitable and releasable therapeutic product can later be manufactured.

limitations: Allele and antigen-processing/display dependencies can limit recognition

records.name: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS)
records.tldr: Organised immune-cell clusters can form within or beside tumours. Their architecture and association with treatment outcomes depend on the study and assay.
records.summary:
Sautès-Fridman and colleagues review tertiary lymphoid structures as organised aggregates of B cells, T cells and dendritic cells that develop in chronically inflamed tissues including tumours, where they are generally associated with longer survival and response to checkpoint inhibitors. Because they are visible on H&E and spatial assays, they are a known-biology probe: a slide or spatial model that recovers TLS is learning something real. No medicine in OnCo is designed to build them. Two linked trials use them directly: a phase 3 trial in triple-negative breast cancer enrols only patients whose residual tumour contains them, and a pancreatic cancer vaccine trial counts how many patients form them as a primary outcome. In the retrospective immune checkpoint cohorts of Vanhersecke et al. (Nature Cancer 2021, PMID 35118423) a structure was called mature when at least one CD23-positive cell with dendritic morphology was found within it, and mature structures were associated with better response rate, progression-free survival and overall survival independently of PD-L1 status and CD8 density; a CD23-positive cell elsewhere in tissue does not establish that architecture. Any TLS were seen in 105 of 328 discovery-cohort cases (32 per cent), 84 of them mature. That is an association in treated cohorts, so it does not by itself show extra benefit from the treatment, and no universal abundance or maturity rule selects a therapy. Aggregate, B-cell follicle and germinal centre are different architectural levels, and an RNA signature alone cannot show a germinal centre. Report density with its area and the criteria used (structures per mm2; two organised structures in 4 mm2 is 0.5 per mm2), because thresholds are method- and study-specific, and small sections or disrupted architecture limit the reading.

Tertiary names where these structures form: ectopic lymphoid organisation in non-lymphoid tissue, including inflamed tissues and tumours. It does not name a cancer stage or establish a particular maturation level.

In untreated invasive breast-tumour specimens, Gu-Trantien and colleagues linked CXCL13-producing follicular helper T cells in TLS germinal centres and an eight-gene signature to group outcomes, including survival or preoperative chemotherapy response. In metastatic melanoma samples, Cabrita and colleagues associated co-occurring CD8-positive T cells and CD20-positive B cells with survival, and a derived TLS signature predicted outcomes in checkpoint-blockade cohorts. Each result retains its specimens, methods and setting; these associations do not establish that inducing a TLS will benefit a particular patient.

records.name: Thymic output and ageing
records.tldr: The thymus can produce new T cells in adulthood. A naive-cell count does not directly measure that output.
records.summary:
Human studies support continued thymic output into adulthood, with age-related decline rather than a fixed birthday shutdown. Existing naive cells can also survive and divide outside the thymus. Human and mouse kinetic studies found different contributions of thymic output and peripheral division; mouse dependence on new output cannot be transferred directly to adult humans.

T-cell receptor excision circles (TRECs) are rearrangement by-products that do not replicate with chromosomes. Peripheral division can dilute measured TREC content. In a fictional closed ledger, 2 cells carrying 4 total circles divide into 4 cells retaining 4 circles: average copies per cell fall from 2 to 1. Allocation can be uneven. This isolates division and does not count new arrivals or daily thymic export. Copies per cell and copies per blood volume have different denominators. Interpret output with survival, division, movement, compartment and timing; naive phenotype, thymic imaging or TREC content alone cannot provide a complete immune-age or cancer-benefit forecast.

notes: Thymic output is release of newly developed T cells; involution is a gradual, variable decline in active tissue rather than a fixed adult-age shutdown. Human age and HIV-treatment measurements support adult output, but no universal individual output rate. Naive-cell maintenance also reflects survival, peripheral division, movement and loss. Human/mouse kinetic comparisons found materially different dependencies; mouse output cannot dictate a human collection or banking rule.

TRECs are circular receptor-rearrangement by-products that do not replicate with chromosomes. In a fictional closed ledger, 2 cells with 4 circles become 4 cells with the same 4 circles: average copies per cell decline from 2 to 1. Daughter pairs can carry 2/0 and 1/1 circles, each retaining the parent's 2. Division alone can dilute copies per cell without proving stopped output. Copies per cell and per blood volume answer different questions; the ledger does not count new arrivals, immune age or daily export.

Naive phenotype is not a recent-emigrant birth certificate. Flow phenotype/counts, kinetic labelling and modelling, receptor sequencing and thymic imaging supply different information; imaging is not a direct daily output count. Interpret measurements with exposure, compartment, observation time, division, survival and movement. Neither more diversity, adult output nor age alone promises a new cancer-recognising receptor, vaccine benefit or a collection recommendation.

records.name: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs)
records.tldr: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes are lymphocytes found in tumour tissue. Their identity, location, measurement denominator and function answer different questions.
records.summary: Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are lymphocytes found in sampled tumour tissue, including T- and B-cell populations. The breast stromal TIL method estimates the area occupied by a defined mononuclear inflammatory infiltrate within eligible tumour-associated stroma on H&E sections. Higher pretreatment scores were associated with better outcomes in the cited early triple-negative breast cancer cohorts, but those associations do not guarantee an individual outcome or establish extra benefit from pembrolizumab. Intratumoral location, stromal area, immune-cell counts and cells expanded for TIL therapy are different measurements or uses.

notes: The breast stromal TIL method estimates the area occupied by mononuclear inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes and plasma cells, as a percentage of eligible tumour-associated stroma. It is not the percentage of all cells, a CD8-cell count or the fraction of cancer cells being killed.

Define the eligible region and treatment setting before estimating the percentage. Use the specified exclusions for normal structures, in-situ disease, necrosis, crush damage and biopsy-site changes, and assess the region overall rather than only its hottest spot. A prognostic association does not establish added benefit from a particular treatment.

In the pooled analysis of 2,148 early-stage TNBC patients given anthracycline-based chemotherapy with or without taxanes, each 10 percentage-point increase in pretreatment stromal TILs corresponded to an adjusted invasive disease-free survival hazard ratio of 0.87 (95% confidence interval 0.83 to 0.91) and overall survival hazard ratio of 0.84 (0.79 to 0.89). These associations do not establish an added pembrolizumab benefit by TIL level.

Among 906 TNBC patients from six neoadjuvant chemotherapy trials, pathological complete response occurred in 80 of 260 with low TILs (0% to 10%), 117 of 373 with intermediate TILs (11% to 59%) and 136 of 273 with high TILs (at least 60%): about 31%, 31% and 50%. These categories describe that analysis and are not universal treatment cutoffs.

Fictional area exercise: region A has 4 units of eligible stroma with 0.4 occupied by infiltrate; region B has 1 unit with 0.6 occupied. Pooled occupied area is (0.4 + 0.6)/(4 + 1) = 20%. Averaging the regional percentages without area weighting gives (10% + 60%)/2 = 35%. This arithmetic illustrates the denominator; it does not prescribe a pixel workflow for clinical semiquantitative scoring.

A fictional sTIL estimate of 30% means that the defined mononuclear infiltrate occupies about 30% of eligible stromal area. It does not mean 30% of all cells are lymphocytes or CD8 cells, or that 30% of cancer cells are being killed. Intratumoral TILs, positive-nucleus fractions, cells per square millimetre and bulk immune RNA measure different things. Additional stains change the measurement rather than silently changing its denominator.

Residual-disease recommendations assess the residual tumour bed rather than simply reusing untreated invasive borders. Keep specimen type, site, treatment setting and observer calibration. A high score does not prove tumour-specific recognition, entry into every malignant nest or a permanent hot-tumour state.

To interpret a stromal TIL estimate, retain the block, sampled site, specimen type and treatment setting, then define the eligible stromal region and its exclusions. The output is a continuous estimated percentage of that area occupied by the specified infiltrate. State whether a trained observer or a computational method produced it, with calibration and regional sampling where relevant. Artifacts, sparse stroma, heterogeneity, observer variation and an unrepresentative sample can limit the result. The section uses finite tissue, and measurement reproducibility is a separate question from validation for clinical treatment selection.

TIL is a location label, CD8 is a phenotype and antigen specificity is another property. Simoni found bystander CD8 cells recognizing viral rather than cancer epitopes in human lung and colorectal tumours; the study’s CD39 associations are not a universal test of every cell’s target. A functional assay compares defined effectors and targets with recognition and target-survival controls. Neither presence, cytokine release nor one killing assay reproduces every access barrier or establishes clinical benefit.

The Loi analysis pooled nine studies. In its node-negative subgroup with at least 30% stromal TILs, three-year overall survival was 99% (95% CI 97% to 100%) after the specified adjuvant chemotherapy. Denkert’s pooled neoadjuvant population contained 3,771 patients overall, including the 906 TNBC patients described above. These population and subgroup findings do not make the study categories universal beneficial-TIL thresholds or establish additional pembrolizumab benefit by score.

In a fictional section, 0.4 square millimetres of mononuclear infiltrate within 2 square millimetres of eligible stroma gives 20% by area. Separately, 30 CD8 cells among 100 counted lymphocytes gives 30% of those counted lymphocytes. Neither is the fraction of all tumour cells, a measure of cancer specificity or evidence of useful killing. One occupied unit among five equal eligible stromal-area units also gives 20%; the drawing illustrates a denominator rather than prescribing pixel counting for semiquantitative breast scoring.

Fixed sections and morphology or selected stains can measure identity, compartment and abundance; viable-cell assays ask about phenotype and function. Dissociation loses native location, culture can select populations and tests consume finite material. Keep cells per square millimetre, specified cell fractions, stromal-area percentages and assay-specific function distinct. TIL therapy is a manufactured expanded-cell product: a tissue count does not establish product yield, composition, potency or treatment success. Sampling, damage, mixed compartments, unsuitable markers and culture selection are different failure modes, and descriptive pathology, research function and clinical treatment selection require different validation.

records.name: Tumour-associated antigen (TAA)
records.tldr: A tumour-associated antigen is a target that is common in a tumour but can also be present in healthy tissue. A treatment aimed at it can affect both, and can also react with a different, look-alike target.
records.summary:
Many tumour-associated antigens come from unmutated proteins, so their usefulness depends on higher expression, an unusual expression pattern or accessibility in the cancer. A neoantigen, by contrast, arises from a tumour-specific sequence alteration. For an antibody or a chimeric antigen receptor, the question is accessible surface antigen on tumour and on healthy cells. For a peptide-directed T-cell receptor it is the particular peptide displayed by a particular HLA allele. RNA for the source gene establishes neither recognition surface, and a gene-expression result does not specify accessibility or peptide display.

Two hazards need different controls. On-target, off-tumour recognition means the receptor recognises its intended target in the wrong tissue. Off-target cross-reactivity means the receptor also recognises a different molecular target, so screening the intended antigen alone cannot rule it out. A published example of the second is an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor directed at HLA-A*01-restricted MAGE-A3: in a clinical study the first two treated patients developed cardiogenic shock and died within days, no MAGE-A3 expression was detected in heart tissue at autopsy, and the T cells recognised an unrelated peptide from the striated-muscle protein titin (Linette et al., 2013; Cameron et al., 2013, who describe the preclinical analysis as having found no off-target concern). That illustrates the hazard for one engineered receptor and is not a toxicity rate for tumour-associated targets. Immune tolerance also shapes the available response to self antigens, and a stronger receptor does not remove the need to test healthy tissues and alternative targets.

A shared antigen can support a treatment intended for more than one person's cancer, with a trade-off between tumour coverage and healthy-tissue exposure; expression prevalence in a cohort is not a safe recognition threshold for a product. For vaccine-elicited peptide-specific T cells, a shared antigen offers another candidate when credible private targets are few, which is a coverage hypothesis, not demonstrated benefit. A peptide from a shared antigen and one from a neoantigen may depend on the same HLA allele, so changing the antigen does not restore a missing display route: Tran et al. (2016) documented escape after loss of the restricting HLA allele in one colorectal cancer patient. Antibodies and CARs have different recognition requirements, and epitope spreading is a separate widening of recognition that adding a shared antigen does not guarantee.

NY-ESO-1 illustrates a shared cancer-testis antigen, rather than a private mutation. Ademuyiwa and colleagues reported immunohistochemical expression in 16% of 168 triple-negative breast cancers and 2% of 47 ER-positive/HER2-negative comparators; the comparison groups had different sampling characteristics, and staining was heterogeneous. Their background describes normal expression restricted to testis. Expression prevalence is neither proof of a displayed peptide on every tumour cell nor evidence that a receptor or vaccine is effective or safe. A shared peptide-directed product still requires the appropriate HLA and functional testing.

Viral proteins provide another possible source of non-self targets, distinct from an altered human protein. NCI identifies HPV as a cause of cervical and oropharyngeal cancers, among other sites. For a proposed viral peptide target, establish viral-protein expression in the relevant cells, compatible peptide-HLA display and receptor recognition. A breast-cancer subtype label alone supplies none of that evidence; it does not establish a viral target or predict benefit from targeting it.

records.name: Tumour microenvironment (TME)
records.tldr: A tumour’s surroundings include cells, vessels, matrix and local conditions. Their presence or location alone does not establish how they affect the cancer or its treatment.
records.summary: Cancer cells interact with neighbouring immune and stromal cells, vessels, extracellular material and physical conditions. These interactions vary across sites, regions and time and can have different consequences. Composition, position, molecular programs and demonstrated function are separate layers of evidence.

The tumour microenvironment includes neighbouring cells, extracellular material, vessels and local physical conditions. A neighbouring cell need not belong to the malignant clone. Cell populations, cytokines and chemokines, matrix, oxygen, nutrients and waste interact in both directions, and their arrangement varies between regions, disease sites and times. A drawing is a map of possible participants, not a measured recipe or a fixed job description.

Keren used multiplexed protein imaging in 41 human triple-negative breast cancers to describe composition and spatial organisation. This is observational evidence. Salmon used viable human lung-tumour slices to investigate matrix and T-cell movement, including a perturbation. The two designs answer different questions, and neither makes stromal removal a universal treatment instruction. Presence or proximity alone does not demonstrate signalling, recognition, killing or suppression.

Retain site, date, treatment, region and denominator: cells per area differs from a fraction of detected cells. Selected-protein imaging, spatial RNA capture with cell assignment and a controlled functional experiment are different outputs. Segmentation can misassign boundaries and dissociation changes which cells are recovered. There is no universal TME score that establishes treatment benefit.

In a fictional macrophage-rich region with inflammatory RNA, composition and expression are observed. The result does not identify every RNA signal’s cellular source, demonstrate macrophage suppression or select the best treatment. A workflow through cells, locations, vessels, matrix and conditions orders questions; it is not a causal chain from cell counts to immune function.
records.analogy: A castle under siege from the inside: the cancer conscripts the town's builders (fibroblasts) to raise walls, bribes the guards (macrophages) to look away, and diverts the water supply (vessels) so that reinforcements (T cells, drugs) never arrive.
